title: Encoder · Google multimodal embeddings
purpose: Develop reusable hosted-provider configuration, adapter, validation and provenance tools that operations and application projects can compose.
boundary: Own the external provider interface and its documented upstream constraints. Cuwacunu and other applications own final integration and application use. Local training, weight access and arbitrary output shapes are not implied; supported configuration follows exposed provider capabilities. Follow the shared encoder component instructions and retain historical provider records and claim limits.
summary: Develop reusable Google multimodal provider tools. The documented Gemini Embedding 2 source has a local provider record; an API adapter and local operation evidence remain proposed. Hosted service capabilities and configuration limits belong to the provider contract, not a finished application.

goals.title: Register and integrate the external provider
goals.description: Use a hosted pretrained model rather than planning foundation-model training; preserve service identity and request provenance.

milestones.title: Document the stable Gemini Embedding 2 provider
milestones.description: The local provider record identifies gemini-embedding-2, official documentation and a proposed 3072-dimensional output contract. A hosted model ID is not an immutable checkpoint identity.
acceptance: README and provider.json identify the selected stable model, supported modalities, official sources and hosted-version limits.
The record explicitly marks the adapter unimplemented, live API unverified and local operation quality unmeasured.

milestones.title: Implement a source-linked multimodal API adapter
milestones.description: Define permissions, credentials, service route, request budget and cache/retry/retention policy before live use. Separate representation configuration from per-call provenance; strengthen the existing response-identity requirement with canonical request and response digests plus retained permitted artifacts, without promising deterministic future service re-execution.
acceptance: The representation contract identifies the requested model, route, returned revision when exposed, declared revision-uncertainty policy, dimensions, normalization, task/role instructions and content-grouping semantics. Per-request and per-response identity is attached to the execution/records rather than creating a unique SpaceRef for every response.

A canonical semantic request manifest covers permitted content digests or immutable source versions, input ordering/grouping, relevant task/role instructions and all effective parameters. Hash the manifest using a specified canonicalization and digest scheme; exclude credentials/secrets and document any protected-content retention constraints.

For each attempt, retain a local execution/attempt ID, request digest, provider response/request ID when actually exposed, explicit absence otherwise, timestamp, returned model/revision metadata when exposed, status and response/artifact digest. Preserve the actual embedding/result artifact needed for offline replay when permitted; retries cannot overwrite earlier attempts.

Distinguish replay of saved response artifacts from a fresh live call. A request hash and response ID alone cannot regenerate an unretained vector or pin an undisclosed provider revision; state that limitation. Fresh responses do not silently enter a frozen corpus/evaluation snapshot; anchor checks can detect some change but do not certify immutable provider identity.

Verify input-to-output grouping/order, shape, finite values, unsupported content, partial batch failures, retries and cache provenance. Declare which task/role pairs are compatible rather than forcing exact task-string equality. No live request is authorized merely by this milestone or by preservation of the provider documentation.

goals.title: Verify multimodal records and operation utility
goals.description: Separate request/shape correctness from retrieval usefulness and composed-operation claims.

milestones.title: Validate a bounded multimodal retrieval fixture
milestones.description: After explicitly admitting permitted inputs and a request budget, preserve a fixed response-artifact snapshot and validate record conformance before assessing bounded cross-modal retrieval. Treat offline replay and fresh-provider execution as different evidence scopes; the documented provider remains locally unverified until actual receipts exist.
acceptance: Resolve the input manifest, supported grouping and task conventions, actual response IDs when exposed, request/response digests, shape/finite-value checks and permitted replay artifacts. Record unsupported content and unavailable revision metadata rather than inventing either.

Use a frozen query/corpus response snapshot, independent relevance definition, baseline and explicit allowed role/space pairs under OR-01; leaked or incompatible entries are rejected with indexed reasons.

Replay the retained pipeline and report task results, uncertainty scope, costs, abstention/partial-failure coverage and provider-version limitations. A successful fixture does not imply general modality support, unchanged future hosted behavior or utility outside its tested population.
No completion is recorded from documentation alone. Adapter correctness, live service verification and operation utility require distinct receipts and must respect foundations-evidence-ledger.

goals.title: Expose Hx18 capabilities as a reusable toolset
goals.description: Develop reusable hosted-provider configuration, encoding, saved-response export/replay and validation tools with documented CLI/library interfaces for operations and applications. Separate provider capability/configuration, request recipe and each execution/result artifact. Preserve service-specific limits and revision uncertainty; Cuwacunu and other applications own final docking. Implemented coverage and remaining gaps must be explicit.

milestones.title: Define the hosted-provider tool surfaces and usage contracts
milestones.description: Map the documented provider, future adapter and selected workflow building blocks into common usage conventions; provider documentation alone establishes no callable implementation or live service verification. The component-tool mission and shared encoder instructions govern this surface definition; a checkpoint or application-specific benchmark is an evidence instance.
acceptance: Inventory the agreed configuration/loading, encoding, saved-response export/replay, validation and workflow surfaces, distinguishing current documentation, implemented interfaces and remaining gaps.

Specify versioned CLI/API inputs and outputs, modality/grouping/task roles, dimensions/normalization, source and request/response identities, actual returned revision metadata or its absence, compatibility requirements and failure/abstention behavior.

Define bounded offline examples, live-call boundaries and completion criteria without assuming immutable hosted weights or universal geometry. Record credential, permitted-content, request-budget and retention requirements before any live execution.

Document which upstream-supported model, modality, dimension, normalization and request options the reusable adapter exposes, their constraints and actual verification coverage. A recorded example response or proposed default does not define every supported configuration; do not promise local weights, fresh model training or shapes the service does not expose.

evidence.label: Hosted provider scope and integration limits

milestones.title: Expose and verify the agreed hosted-provider building blocks
milestones.description: Deliver the agreed provider tools, reusable interfaces and bounded integration examples, reporting saved-response replay separately from any explicitly admitted live requests. Coverage must demonstrate the agreed reusable component contract and state configuration/training or provider limitations explicitly.
acceptance: Expose the agreed hosted-provider building blocks through documented Linux CLI and reusable library interfaces in the managed container, using common provider records while keeping service-specific configuration, request handling and export in the provider component.

Verify selected standalone tools and a bounded provider-to-operation workflow, including grouping/order, native shape, provenance, unsupported content, partial failures, retries/cache identity and incompatible consumer cases; retain replay limits and unknown provider revisions explicitly.

Retain actual engineering receipts and examples with explicit offline/live coverage and gaps. Keep credentials and restricted content private; live API requests and utility evaluations require their actual permitted inputs, budget, protocol and permissions.

Verify representative supported provider configurations through reusable adapter/validation interfaces and bounded offline fixtures or separately admitted live calls. Record unavailable capabilities and configuration limits explicitly; the deliverable is a composable provider tool, while application docking and end-to-end utility remain separate.
